Mark the student's response to a question from the 2025 NSW HSC Ancient History exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting. The images attached before this text are the sources the question refers to, in letter order; read them and judge how well the response uses them. Judge the response the way HSC Ancient History markers do: a direct answer to the question, a sustained judgement where the directive verb asks for one, specific and accurate evidence (dates, names, cases, legislation, sources, historians) and the terms of the course. Do not reward length or narrative for its own sake.

Question 4 [12 marks]: How have new technologies contributed to an understanding of Pompeii and Herculaneum?
Support your answer using evidence from Sources C and D and other relevant sources.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 12):
10–12 marks: Provides a well-developed and informed explanation of how new technologies have contributed to an understanding of Pompeii and Herculaneum | Integrates evidence from Sources C and D and other relevant sources to support the response | Uses a range of appropriate historical terms and concepts
7–9 marks: Provides an informed explanation of how new technologies have contributed to an understanding of Pompeii and Herculaneum | Uses evidence from Sources C and D and other relevant source(s) to support the response | Uses appropriate historical terms and concepts
4–6 marks: Provides an explanation of how new technologies have contributed to an understanding of Pompeii and/or Herculaneum | Refers to Sources C and/or D and may refer to other source(s) | Uses some appropriate historical terms and concepts
1–3 marks: Makes general statement(s) about new technology and its use in the study of Pompeii and/or Herculaneum | May refer to Source C and/or Source D and/or other source(s)


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
• New DNA evidence from skeletons has revealed details about the genetic origins, health, and diets of the inhabitants, deepening our understanding of their daily lives and connections to other Mediterranean populations. (Source C)
• Advanced AI technology has enabled researchers to virtually ‘unroll’ charred scrolls from Herculaneum, revealing previously inaccessible texts and providing insights into the intellectual life of the ancient world. (Source D)
• Ground-Penetrating Radar (GPR): This technology has mapped hidden structures beneath volcanic deposits, identifying buildings and streets without the need for invasive excavation. This has informed understanding of the nature of the eruption and its impact.
• 3D Reconstruction: Digital modelling and 3D reconstructions have allowed researchers to recreate homes, temples, and shops, offering immersive views of how these cities looked before the eruption.
• Chemical Analysis: Portable X-ray fluorescence (pXRF) and other techniques have analysed frescoes, pottery, and residues, shedding light on trade networks, local craftsmanship, and diet.
• CT scans of plaster casts have revealed further information on the identities of people who died, providing insights into the population of Pompeii and who remained behind.
